I have completed an independent review of the ward handover application and recorded the release verdict in [REVIEW.md](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-QliU69/workspace/REVIEW.md).

### What Was Verified
1. **Automated Acceptance & Operability**: Executed the `product-acceptance` checker script (`accept-check.js`), which resulted in a `BLOCK` verdict due to missing operational documentation and health check endpoints.
2. **Automated Unit & Integration Tests**: Executed `npm test`, confirming the test suite consists of only a single unit test for `renderNote` and lacks coverage for authentication, API routes, ward access control, and persistence.
3. **Application & Codebase Audit**:
   - **Frontend UI**: Verified that `public/index.html` contains no script or CSS assets to render the user interface described in [ux-walkthrough.md](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-QliU69/workspace/ux-walkthrough.md).
   - **Authentication & Sessions**: Audited [src/server.js](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-QliU69/workspace/src/server.js#L8-L10) and identified that missing cookie-parsing middleware causes `req.cookies` to remain `undefined`, breaking all authenticated endpoints (`401 no_session`).
   - **Authorization Boundaries**: Verified that `GET /api/notes` allows `req.query.ward` to override session ward scoping, exposing cross-ward patient handover notes to any authenticated user.
   - **Data Integrity & Persistence**: Audited [src/store.js](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-QliU69/workspace/src/store.js#L8) and confirmed that server startup executes a destructive `fs.writeFileSync` call that wipes all stored handover notes.

**Release Verdict**: **BLOCK (Do Not Ship)**
